utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I do understand that there's a question as to how the order will be, but let's perhaps discuss that once you, Mr. Kearney, have finished your examination-in-chief of Witness 62. Witness 62, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Kearney will now continue his examination. Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 62, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When we broke yesterday, you made a statement that I want to follow-up on. You were asked by myself at page 5569, line 9, the following question: "Now, did these accusations or -- of your being a spy or a traitor for the Serbs persist after 1992"? And you gave the following answer which I want to follow-up on. You said yesterday: "Yes. Things were said in the village. This was their propaganda, I mean the propaganda of the families with whom I was in this feud according to the Kanun, but also during the war." And I want to follow-up with you. When you said "also during the war," what time-period were you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke with him about the period 1998/1999.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Since we are back in open session now, the Chamber has just now decided that the sequence -- the order of cross-examination is that the Chamber starts with the cross-examination of Witness 62, and only once we have finished the cross-examination of Witness 62, Defence counsel will have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness that was -- the witness that testified before, that is Miomir Stosic. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 62, I want to start, if I may, by asking you some questions about the two conversations that you had with Din Krasniqi in Vranoc about the disappearance of your parents on the 14th and 15th of July, that is, the conversations that took place on the 14th and 15th of July. I'm going to ask you a little bit more about these conversations later on, but for now I just want to ask you about one part of your evidence in relation to those conversations. And you told Mr. Kearney, for the Prosecution, that you had said to Din Krasniqi that you believed the disappearance of your parents was connected with a long-running blood-feud which your family had become involved in. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it also correct that it has always been your strong belief that your parents' death was a measure of revenge connected with that blood-feud?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, my parents, when they were taken away, I believed that Rrustem Tetaj had taken them so that they could give him information who had injured my brother. Later on, I had suspicions a couple of days later, after their abduction. So I had this suspicion that this was a measure of revenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think when you made your witness statement in 2006 - and this is the first line of paragraph 37 - the words you used were these: "I strongly believe that my parents were abducted as a measure of revenge." And was that an accurate statement of what your belief was in 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it earlier, that in the beginning Rrustem Tetaj had taken them so that he could be informed about the case. Later on when I heard that who was involved in that circle, then I had the suspicion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll come back to Rrustem Tetaj in a little while. Can I just explore with you briefly some of the background to that blood-feud and some of the personalities involved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I take it that there comes a moment soon where we have to turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, there does, and I think we may have reached that moment at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we should turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are then in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We then also could have the break if you move to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We need the full half hour because for technical reasons. We'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just a very brief matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And really just a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Emmerson, until it is confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Where it was announced before the break that we would continue with the cross-examination in open session, the Chamber, in view of the effectiveness of protective measures has decided that we'll continue in private session. We return to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 62, I want to ask you a question that was just posed by the Court. In your opinion what would happen to people that were considered to be collaborators?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the same question --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And asking in terms of an opinion. If there are specific instances that Mr. Kearney seeks to elicit, then I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I can rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What happened to people in 1998 during the war who were considered to be collaborators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At -- this is what happened to my parents. They paid it dearly. I do not need to speak about other people. The example is my parents. So the slander, the slander, due to the slander they do not exist today, no matter what you could refer to as revenge or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You had mentioned that these allegations of collaboration against your family had been going on for some time. I want to ask you if in 1998 during the war those allegations increased or decreased or stayed the same in terms of their number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the abduction of my parents, they did not increase, the rumours decreased. And with deeds I proved that the slander were simply slander and that they were made by the enemies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me be more specific, Witness Number 62. I want to ask you about the period of time before your parents were abducted in 1998. Did the level of allegations against your family increase, decrease, or stay the same at that time compared with the previous years of the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998 there were rumours, probably more than in the period from 1992 to 1998. However, after the abduction of my parents, for about one month after that -- and after that there was a different realisation. People understood the mistake. They understood that that was a false propaganda, because we as a family, we contributed, probably not with weapons but with the hospitality, accommodation, by also following the instructions of the armed group, of the UCK. I collaborated with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about the family of Qaush Krasniqi, specifically his mother and his two siblings who were abducted and murdered in October of 1998. You mentioned that there had been fights between two families before that abduction. Is that a fair statement of your earlier testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith, may I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you would like to have the question rephrased that they were abducted and found killed? Or found dead --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps that was not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be my -- that I've overlooked something. Certainly in the paragraph in the witness statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- it simply says that they are missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. That's perhaps then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, to be very specific I can read directly this witness's answer on cross-examination if I can -- if that will help with the proceeding of this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is at page 32, I believe, I'm going to read a quote for you from an answer you gave. "For example, if we have an argument together if we have a fight, then that means that I can take revenge on you or you can take revenge on me so this is a situation." I want to ask you simply regarding the fights that the family of Qaush Krasniqi engaged in. Were the fights that they had engaged in a sufficient basis under the Kanun to justify the abduction and murder of three members of the family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but not to do as they did. They were taken in order to take revenge but also to put a blemish on the family but also to the UCK. So these are three weak points. If you take revenge, then I would be punished. This is -- then they would also say that the UCK did this and then UCK would come under such accusation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I said I would not have a break any earlier than 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I have no further question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've been alerted to what may be an extremely important error in translation. I don't know whether Your Honour wants me to deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it was an issue that we need to trouble the witness with. It's simply an issue of clarifying with the interpreters what, in fact, was said so it needn't detain the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off for a second then. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Page 64, line 12, the answer reads: "Avdi was the commander in the village, the commander of the UCK. Brahim was like a leader, the leader of the village. He was in charge of the organisation of the civilian population. So these two people were directly engaged in the village. It was Ramush Haradinaj, it was also FARK in that area, but these two people belonged to the UCK." I understand that the original Albanian properly translated and transcribed would read something closer to: I don't know who was connected to FARK and who was connected to Ramush, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's more or less how I understood --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- this translation, that is, you had Haradinaj, you had the FARK, but these two at least were UCK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Maybe the simplest thing would be if I made a request to check the tape overnight and if there's any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes and I -- but would that be a reason to keep the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then clear. Any further questions? No. Then Judge Hoepfel has a question for you. Could you put up -- put on your earphones again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 62, Judge Hoepfel has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Witness, may I get back to that what you commented just before when asked if such fights would be a sufficient basis under the Kanun to justify the abduction and murder of three members of a family. Do you remember this question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And your answer was: "It could be, but not to do as they did," or not in the way they did I suppose you wanted to say. Can you explain yourself a little more precise -- precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/62 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the Kanun, children and females are not involved in the killing or in the -- being killed. It's males from 18 to 65 years old that are involved in the blood-feud. If you kill a child or a female instead of taking revenge, you owe blood to them two times. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Trial Chamber's extreme permission, that was a -- the last question by Judge Hoepfel to the witness was very insightful. And there was a very important answer given back by the witness. I would be -- I would ask leave just to follow-up on it with just one question if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, the Chamber decided that we'll not allow you to put further questions to the witness. It's not a matter that could not have been raised by yourself at any earlier moment. Witness 62, since the Chamber takes it that no further questions will be put to you because the Chambers questions have not triggered any need for the Defence to ask further questions to you, this means that this concludes your evidence in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming and for answering all questions put to you. You are free to go again. I wish you a safe trip home. If you could stay there just for a second, because I would like to ask something to the Defence. How much time do you think you could finish if we resume at five or ten minutes after 6.00? Do you think the cross-examination of the next witness could be finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn until ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stosic. You had to wait for a while, but we're now ready to continue. Mr. Stosic, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. You'll now be cross-examined first by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stosic, I'm going to be asking you some questions from your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder whether I might ask Mr. Registrar to be loading P342 whilst I ask my first questions. Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us yesterday, Mr. Stosic, that you went to the Lake Radoniq canal and that sometime shortly after that you went to the Hotel Pashtrik. I want to see if I can identify with you some dates. Can you remember now roughly how long before you went to Hotel Pashtrik it was that you went to the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if I tell you that the records show that you were at Hotel Pashtrik identifying your father's remains on the 14th of September, does that mean that the visit to the canal must have been no later than about the 9th or 10th?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you got to the canal area, you told us that you saw some police vehicles, some fire brigade vehicles, and some civilian vehicles. Can I ask you, please, about the civilian vehicles. Do you remember how many there were, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, would it have been more or less than ten?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less than ten, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And more or less than five, can you help us, or not?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please speak louder so the interpreters can hear you, and could you please repeat your last answer, that is, more or less than five?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot give you an answer to that question. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And again, with police vehicles, can you give us a sense at all of the number of police vehicles that were there or not?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you recall whether there were any areas taped-off, that is to say with tapes around them, to indicate which areas people were permitted to enter and which they weren't?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me just clarify that answer please, if I may. Were there tapes, were there areas taped-off, with tape?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the area was taped-off.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Looking at the photograph there --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I don't know whether the usher might assist. There's no difficulty, I think, with adding additional marks to the photograph if it remains at the same scale. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that the photograph has been admitted into evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so what we could do is to -- starting with this one --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and make it a new exhibit. That means that the already marked photograph would then be further marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then I would suggest we take a further colour for any further markings. But once we start marking we can't change the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we can't zoom-in or zoom-out anymore. Therefore, I take it that you want to work on the basis of the photograph as it is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly as it is now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then could another colour be given to the witness. Please proceed. Mr. Registrar the map now to be marked would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be marked for identification as D116.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stosic, can you now recall looking at that photograph before you mark it, can you now recall which areas were taped-off?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult, but I will try.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could then please mark the photograph as best you can with a line to show where the tape was.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does that indicate that you could not enter the area to the left of the blue line that you have drawn?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you again. You've drawn a blue line on the photograph. Does that blue line represent a line of tape, as you remember it, that was there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. But just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the previous question, no one could ever consider that the whole other area would be taped off --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so therefore logic is the response to your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think for the sake of the record I had sorted it out, but I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, ever enter the area to the left of the blue line yourself or not?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally on this part of my questions, can I ask you to confirm, were there police divers present when you were at the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you remember making a statement in this case in May of 2002 to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On page 3 of your statement at the very bottom, last few words on the page, you've indicated that the police had underwater divers at the location. Does that assist you with your memory at all?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I want you, if you wouldn't mind, just to concentrate very closely on the questions I'm about to ask you about locations within the canal. In the witness statement that you made in 2002 on page 4 in the second paragraph, after you describe the car that was in the canal and the bodies that were there, you say this of the bodies, you say: "Some were slightly covered with dirt and others buried deeper under the silt of the canal." So you say: "Some were slightly covered with dirt and others were buried deeper under the silt of the canal." Now, Mr. Stosic, we can see from the photograph that there's a concrete section of the canal and that lower down there is a natural section where we can see a river-bed. When you were describing in your statement the fact that there were bodies -- that there were bodies deeper under the silt of the canal, can you help us, please, were you referring to silt in the natural section of the canal or in the concrete section?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were on the slope of the canal. From the part that was in concrete, there was a sort of slope and they were up. They were not in the silt in that part, that's not where the bodies were. They were from the concrete section of the canal upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you mark perhaps with a number 1 on the photograph where those bodies that you're referring to were, please. Could you mark the photograph with a 1, number 1 for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So just to return to your statement, if I can just remind you what you say there. You say that: "Some were slightly covered with dirt and others buried deeper under the silt of the canal." Can you help us whether you were referring only to bodies that were in that area or also bodies lower down in that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part of the canal that was covered with concrete, that's where the bodies were. But then further down along the canal there were a couple of bodies, and you could see them from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's what I was asking you. And were those ones further down, were they the bodies that you referred to as being deeper under the silt of the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain. They were along the direction of the canal, from the concrete part of the canal downwards, near the river -- near the water.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'm looking again at your witness statement on page 4 and the second full paragraph, where you described your visit to Hotel Pashtrik to identify your father's remains and you say this, you say: "I could only positively identify his clothing, as the flesh was gone from his face. His body had been found deeper in the silt of the canal." Now, first of all, how did you know that his body had been found deeper in the silt of the canal? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the people said who were doing the autopsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And by "deeper in the silt of the canal," do you mean in the natural section of the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this top part. But since the bodies were on top of each other they explain that he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- lower down and the others were on top over.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Did you, yourself, go down into the natural section of the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that you assisted with the removal of that red car from the canal with ropes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon, do you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A transcript reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- a transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you and the people you were with manage to get the car out of the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we managed to pull it along the side, not all the way up the bank, but we kind of managed to get it out of the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you left it by the side of the water but at the bottom of the canyon section - is that the position - you didn't pull it up?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all the way up, just along the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your witness statement, you refer to the fact that there was a body in the boot of the car. Can I ask you, do you now remember seeing a body in the boot of the car?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you present when the boot was opened?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of your testimony yesterday, you referred to two other places that you had visited where bodies had been discovered. The first was Zlopek and you told us - this is transcript 5503, line 24 - that although you weren't sure about the date, you thought it was about a month and a half after your father disappeared that you went to Zlopek. Does that sound right to you? Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that would put your visit to Zlopek sometime around the end of August or early September. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And whilst in Zlopek, you saw the recovery of the body of an Albanian man who had been found in a pond. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, help recover that body out of the water?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you left the scene in Zlopek, was the body still there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it stayed. I left and the body was left behind. We were waiting for the car or the transport to take it where it was supposed to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you where it was going to be taken?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think the translation has come through, although the answer is basically clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your answer that whether anyone told you where it was going to be taken, that body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the other place that you described visiting where you saw bodies being recovered was Lumbardh. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that you went to Lumbardh on the same day as you went to the canal and after you had been to the canal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I went to the canal, then to Ljumbard, and then again back to the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at Lumbardh, you saw four bodies, two men and two woman. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they established, that there were four bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see the bodies yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- they were not bodies, they were just body parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So they were in a state of decomposition. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decomposing, also tampered with by animals. Half the bodies were missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, at the time you went to the canal that day, you told us yesterday that you saw five or six bodies there. Is that an accurate reflection of your memory, that you saw five or six bodies in all at the canal when you were there, or could there have been more than that?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the question, I'm afraid, is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Unambiguous, whether there were more or whether the witness saw more.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stosic, just for the sake of clarity it's my fault for asking a question that wasn't as clear as it could have been. You yourself only saw five to six bodies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, going back to the bodies or the body parts at Lumbardh, again, when you left Lumbardh were those body parts still there or had they been removed?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'm sorry to jump about a little, but whilst you were at the canal that day did you talk to any of the officials that were there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have the interpretation louder, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you assist the witness in having the volume of his earphones adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question. Whilst you were at the canal, did you talk to any of the officials that were there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have heard and seen certain records in this case that indicate that some body parts were recovered from an area of rough ground close to a road near the village of Dashinoc. First of all, do you know where Dashinoc is?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dashinoc, that belongs to Ljumbarda, that's how we used to refer to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember whether anybody discussed with you moving bodies that had been recovered from other areas like Lumbardh, like Dashinoc, like Zlopek, to the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. Nobody talked to me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that certain remains had been found in or near Dashinoc?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about the remains, that they had been found. Now, what was done with them later, I don't know. I guess they were all transported to the Pastrik Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be clear. At Lumbardh -- are you suggesting that the area that you visited in Lumbardh was potentially the site at which in remains were recovered in Dashinoc?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were told, were you, that from what had been recovered it was possible to determine that there were two men and two women there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that something that -- I'm sorry, did we get the response to that? We did, we did. Thank you. And was that something that you were told there and then at the site?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that it was said to me, it's just that I overheard a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that conversation was at the site itself?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the final topic I want to ask you about is this, you gave some evidence to Mr. Di Fazio yesterday about the tensions in the area around Loxha during this period of time and the risks involved in moving around. I just want to clarify one or two issues with you about dates. The date that you have given is the date that your father left home, heading for Loxha, is the 17th of July. Can I ask you how certain you are of the correctness of that date?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you aware of the fact that there had been intense fighting around Loxha at various points during July?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no fights at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that there had been a three-day battle around Loxha in the first part of July?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Obviously, if you don't know, I'm not asking you to speculate. Is the position that you simply don't know one way or the other what the state of fighting was in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not that. It's just that I know that there was no fighting going on at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know when the fighting was taking place at Loxha during July?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. It could have been even beginning of August or late July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I make it absolutely clear, I'm not asking you to guess. "It could have been" obviously is a phrase that leaves a lot of things open to speculation. If you don't know, then please say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you do know or not. You said,"not first part of July," then you said later,"could have been end of July, early August." Do you know? Because if you are uncertain about it, then please tell us then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was definitely no fighting at around mid-July. It could have been late July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stosic, we have certain reports of fighting in various parts of the region, including reports of fighting in Loxha on the 21st of July, for example. Now, if you're telling us that you hadn't been to Loxha, I just want to be clear whether you are in a position to say one way or the other whether at around that time there was fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting going on, but there was none before the 17th. That's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, that's why I wanted to just ask you about your certainty about the date. Because when you gave evidence yesterday - this is transcript 5498, line 15 - you were asked for the date that you last saw your father and you said: "The 17th of July, as far as I can recall." Now, in the evidence you've just given us you tell us you're certain of that date. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because in the witness statement that you made about your father in May 2002, Mr. Stosic, this is page 2, last paragraph, you say that the date on which you last saw him was the 19th of July. Again, a day or two's difference may be important, Mr. Stosic. Can I ask you again, please: How sure are you of the exact date?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it was the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us as to why you signed a statement to the Prosecution in May 2002 saying it was the 19th? Has something happened in between to make you sure of the date?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I made a mistake when giving the statement; however, I'm certain that it was the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I -- just so that we're clear, why are you certain? What is it that makes you certain?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because I reported it to the Red Cross and to the Secretariat of the Interior, that's the date I reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be right. Do you have those reports yourself still?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But did you keep a note of the date that you made them, or the date that your father disappeared in some other document?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I kept the document which is in Serbia, it's in the papers. The photograph was published, and I still have to this day the -- a report in the papers with his picture and information about him having gone missing and that we were looking for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Stosic, I don't want to take time with you over this, but we have a record that indicates that you reported your father missing in a report to Interpol and gave them the date of the 18th of July. Now, I'm just asking you again: How certain are you of your dates?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain because he went missing on the 17th, and it was on the following day that I reported it to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear the report indicates that the date on which you last saw your father, as you reported, it was the 18th, not that the report was made on the 18th. Mr. Stosic, when you made your witness statement to the Prosecution in May 2002, you gave as the date of your identification process at the Hotel Pashtrik the 17th or 18th of September. And as I indicated to you a little earlier, the records show that it was, in fact, the 14th of September. Again, just to be clear, are you and have you been somewhat vague in your memory of these specific dates?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that on the 17th or 18th I attended the identification process and took over the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but as I'm indicating to you the records show that that took place on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if the witness -- If Your Honours please, the witness has said it and repeatedly now, this is really a matter that is a question for submission --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He can repeatedly say it to the witness, and he can repeatedly gives his answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll take the point, and I think that I've taken the line questioning as far as I need to, and those are the only questions I have for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Stosic, you'll now be examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who is counsel for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to go back to the time you were at the canal and if I understand your testimony correctly you were at the canal on two separate occasions on the same date. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time, the first time that you were there, can you tell us how long a period of time you were at the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And was it during that period of time that you helped pull the car out?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The second time that you went to the canal, could you tell us when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what time it was. It was in the afternoon, but I don't know what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you give us an indication of how long you were at the canal the second time you were there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, perhaps an hour, not more than that definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you first saw the car that you helped pull out of the canal, it was upside down; right?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the half an hour period that you were there, you, along with others, were able to pull the car out of the canal and turn it over so it was right-side up. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the half an hour period that you were there --

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But later on I returned. I didn't touch anything during the first half an hour. It's upon my return --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you are creating confusion. The witness testified that the first time he went there he was there for half an hour, and for the second time he said, I don't know exactly, but not more than one hour. By referring to the half-hour again and again --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My apologies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I didn't mean to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The second time that you were there when you helped pull the car out of the canal, how long a period of time were you involved in that endeavour, pulling the car out of the canal?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were already working and they needed some help, so I approached them and helped them. They had already been working on pulling it out, and I wasn't there the entire time. I just came towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So the second time you went to the canal, did you return to the area where you had first seen the car upside down earlier that day?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you assisted in pulling the car out of the canal the second time, was the body still in the trunk of the car?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were able to assist everybody in moving the car to the side of the canal; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions for the witness. Mr. Di Fazio, is there any need to re-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: A few. I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the clock -- could you keep it short.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll wrap it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: A very limited topic, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were asked questions this afternoon about your visit to Zlopek and -- or Lumbardh and when bodies were being -- or remains were being found. I want to know if you can tell us the sorts of persons that were present on those locations. Firstly, were there police present?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At both Zlopek and Lumbardh?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any court officials present?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At both places?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember concerning Zlopek. As for Ljumbarda -- actually, yes, in both cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So we've got police, we've got court officials present at both locations. What about soldiers, VJ soldiers, were there any soldiers present at those locations?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you remember any other category of official, other than police and court officials, at Zlopek and Lumbardh?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were perhaps another two civilians there looking for their relatives, a brother, a cousin, they were there with me during the identification process.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. So you've got police, court officials, civilians, such as yourself, concerned civilians. Thank you. And about how many individuals all together would you say were at Zlopek when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including the police or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All together. Court officials, police, and civilians, about how many people would you say were at Zlopek?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 15 to 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about Lumbardh, about how many people all together were present there?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps only five to six.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there people with cameras at Zlopek?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, yes, there was a technician recording this. I don't remember for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Okay. You're unsure about that. Can you tell us if you saw any official -- anyone operating a camera, either a movie camera or an ordinary camera, at the second place -- at the other place at Lumbardh?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I think yesterday page 5503 question -- yes, previous page: "Were there any cameras there? "Yes. "Who operated the camera technicians, do you know?" So therefore those questions have been put to the witness already.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honours for reminding me it was superfluous in those circumstances, and if Your Honours please I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Have they triggered -- Mr. Stosic, I would have one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you said there were court officials, how did you know that these persons were court officials?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know one of them personally by sight. I know that he's a public prosecutor. He was there with me, and he was the one making a record, the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was that both at Zlopek and Ljumbarda that he was present?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zlopek, yes. As for Ljumbarda, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how did you know in Ljumbarda that persons present there were court officials?

utterances.speaker: MIOMIR STOSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can see that that this is a person from a court and there was also a note-taker and a person in uniform. They were writing everything down, recording everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Stosic, this concludes your testimony in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes your testimony in this court. We'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, it's quite a journey, and for answering all questions put to you. And I wish you a safe trip home again. And then, finally, the map again marked now with blue, no objections, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, if you would remind me what the number was, then I can admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D116.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit D116 is admitted into evidence. We adjourn. We'll resume tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
